channel.title: FixMyError.net – Recently Added Errors
channel.description: Newly added developer and infrastructure error fixes on FixMyError.net.

item.title: Apache: AH00161: server reached MaxRequestWorkers setting, consider raising
item.description: Every Apache worker is busy, so new connections wait in the listen queue and the site slows down or hangs. Raising the limit treats the symptom; the real question is what is holding the workers. Under the prefork MPM with mod_php, each request ties up a whole process for as long as a slow PHP…

item.title: API Gateway: {"message": "Endpoint request timed out"}
item.description: API Gateway stopped waiting for the integration, which for REST APIs happens at 29 seconds by default whatever the Lambda function's own timeout says. A function set to five minutes keeps running and finishes successfully in CloudWatch, but its answer is thrown away and the client gets a 504. HTTP…

item.title: Auth.js: UntrustedHost: Host must be trusted. URL was: http://localhost:3000
item.description: Auth.js (NextAuth v5) will not build callback URLs from a Host header it has not been told to trust, which protects against host header injection. On Vercel and under next dev it trusts the host automatically, so the error first appears with next start, in Docker or behind your own reverse proxy…

item.title: AWS Lambda: Response payload size exceeded maximum allowed payload size
item.description: Synchronous invocations have a fixed 6 MB limit on the response (and on the request), and it cannot be raised. Your code ran to completion: the error is raised after the handler returns, which is why the function logs look clean. Behind API Gateway the practical limit is lower still, because…

item.title: AWS Lambda: Runtime.InvalidEntrypoint (exec format error)
item.description: Lambda could not start the container image's entrypoint at all. When the detail says exec format error, the image was built for a different CPU from the function: an image built on an Apple silicon Mac is arm64, and a function created with the default x86_64 architecture cannot run it. The same…

item.title: Composer detected issues in your platform: Your Composer dependencies require
item.description: Since Composer 2, vendor/composer/platform_check.php runs on every request and stops the app if the PHP running it is older than the locked packages need. The trap is two PHP binaries: composer install ran under CLI PHP 8.3 (in CI or on your laptop) while the web server runs PHP-FPM 8.1, so php -v…

item.title: Dart: type 'List<dynamic>' is not a subtype of type 'List<String>'
item.description: jsonDecode always returns plain List and Map objects, whatever the JSON holds, and Dart will not reinterpret a List as a List just because every element happens to be a string. The failure comes from an implicit cast, such as assigning json['tags'] to a List field, so it compiles cleanly and only…

item.title: Flutter: Binding has not yet been initialized.
item.description: Something used a platform channel (Firebase.initializeApp, SharedPreferences, path_provider, a SystemChrome call) before runApp, and runApp is what normally creates the binding those channels depend on. Making main() async and awaiting setup work first is exactly what triggers it. The fix is one…

item.title: Flutter: Unable to load asset: "assets/images/logo.png"
item.description: The file is on disk but not in the app bundle, because Flutter only packages what pubspec.yaml lists under flutter: assets:. Usual causes: YAML indentation (assets: must sit two spaces under flutter:, not at the top level), a folder listed without its trailing slash, or expecting a folder entry to…

item.title: Keycloak: Invalid token issuer. Expected 'http://keycloak:8080/realms/myrealm'
item.description: The token's iss claim comes from whichever hostname the client used to reach Keycloak, and something later checked it against a different one. The classic case is Docker Compose: the browser logs in through http://localhost:8080, the backend validates against http://keycloak:8080, and the two…

item.title: Laravel: Vite manifest not found at: /var/www/public/build/manifest.json
item.description: The @vite directive reads public/build/manifest.json to find the hashed asset filenames, and that file only exists after npm run build. So this is not really a PHP problem. Either the front-end build never ran in this environment (a deploy that only runs composer install, or a Docker image with no…

item.title: macOS: zsh: bad CPU type in executable
item.description: The binary contains only Intel x86_64 code, and this Mac has an Apple silicon chip without Rosetta 2 installed. macOS offers to install Rosetta when you open an Intel app from the Finder, but a binary started from the terminal, a script or a CI runner just fails with this. It also catches old…

item.title: Microsoft Entra ID: AADSTS9002326: Cross-origin token redemption is permitted
item.description: The browser swapped the authorisation code for tokens itself, with a fetch that carries an Origin header, but the redirect URI is registered under the Web platform, which Entra treats as a server-side confidential client. MSAL.js 2 and later always does this from the browser using PKCE, so the URI…

item.title: nginx: [emerg] "proxy_cache" zone "my_cache" is unknown
item.description: proxy_cache refers to a shared memory zone that only exists once a proxy_cache_path line declares it with keys_zone=, and nginx found no zone with that name. Usually the server block was copied from another machine without the proxy_cache_path line that lived in that machine's nginx.conf, or the…

item.title: nginx: [emerg] cannot load certificate "/etc/ssl/my.crt": BIO_new_file() failed
item.description: nginx could not open the certificate file at all, before reading a byte of it, so this is about the file and not the certificate. The end of the message tells you which. No such file or directory usually means a Let's Encrypt path for a certificate that was never issued, or a symlink in live/…

item.title: nginx: rewrite or internal redirection cycle while internally redirecting to
item.description: Logged alongside a 500 when a try_files fallback or a rewrite sends nginx back into a location that falls back again, until it gives up after ten internal redirects. In a single-page app the usual cause is try_files $uri $uri/ /index.html where index.html is not actually in root: the root path is…

item.title: PHP: Fatal error: Uncaught Error: Call to undefined function mysqli_connect()
item.description: PHP cannot find the function because the mysqli extension is not loaded in the PHP that ran the script. MySQL itself is not involved yet. Distributions ship extensions as separate packages (php8.3-mysql on Debian and Ubuntu, php-mysqlnd on RHEL), and the CLI and PHP-FPM read different php.ini…

item.title: Postfix: connect to mx1.example.net[203.0.113.25]:25: Connection timed out
item.description: Your server never got a TCP connection to the recipient's mail server on port 25, so the message sits deferred in the queue. If it happens for every destination, the remote side is almost never at fault: most cloud providers block outbound port 25 by default (Google Cloud, Azure, AWS and many VPS…

item.title: Postfix: SASL authentication failure: No worthy mechs found
item.description: Postfix tried to log in to the relay and Cyrus SASL could not find a mechanism the relay accepts. The username and password are not the problem. Either the plugin package is missing (libsasl2-modules on Debian and Ubuntu, cyrus-sasl-plain on RHEL), so PLAIN and LOGIN do not exist at all, or the…

item.title: PowerShell: WARNING: Unable to resolve package source
item.description: Windows PowerShell 5.1 runs on .NET Framework, which on older or unpatched systems still offers only TLS 1.0 and 1.1 by default, and the PowerShell Gallery has required TLS 1.2 since 2020. The handshake fails, so Install-Module reports the gallery as unreachable even though a browser on the same…

item.title: Proxmox: TASK ERROR: KVM virtualisation configured, but not available
item.description: The VM is set to use hardware acceleration (kvm: 1, the default) but the host has no /dev/kvm. On bare metal that means Intel VT-x or AMD-V is switched off in the firmware settings. When Proxmox is itself running as a VM, say a home lab under VMware, Hyper-V or another Proxmox, the outer…

item.title: Rails: ActiveRecord::NoDatabaseError: We could not find your database
item.description: Rails reached the database server and logged in, but the database it asked for does not exist there. That rules out the host and the password. On a fresh clone, a new CI runner or a new Docker volume nobody has run db:create yet, or DATABASE_URL points at a server where the database has a…

item.title: Rails: Blocked hosts: myapp.example.com
item.description: This is Rails' own HostAuthorization middleware, added in Rails 6 to stop DNS rebinding attacks, refusing a Host header that is not in config.hosts. In development only localhost, .localhost and IP addresses are allowed, so it appears the first time you use an ngrok tunnel, a Codespaces URL or a…

item.title: Redis: BUSY Redis is busy running a script
item.description: Redis runs Lua scripts and functions atomically on its single main thread, so while one runs nothing else is served. After busy-reply-threshold (called lua-time-limit before Redis 7, 5 seconds by default) Redis answers every other client with BUSY, but it does not stop the script. The usual…

item.title: SMTP: 534-5.7.9 Application-specific password required
item.description: Gmail accepted the connection but will not take the account's normal password over SMTP, because the account has 2-Step Verification turned on. Since Google ended less secure app access in 2024, a plain password does not work for SMTP, IMAP or POP at all (without 2-Step Verification you get…

item.title: Spring: java.lang.IllegalArgumentException: Cannot find cache named 'users'
item.description: A @Cacheable, @CachePut or @CacheEvict annotation names a cache that the CacheManager does not know and will not create. Spring Boot's default simple cache creates caches on demand, so everything works until a real provider arrives: Caffeine with spring.cache.cache-names set, or a JCache provider…

item.title: Svelte 5: `$:` is not allowed in runes mode, use `$derived` or `$effect` instead
item.description: As soon as a component uses any rune ($state, $props, $derived), Svelte compiles the whole file in runes mode, and the old $: reactive statements stop being valid. So adding one $state to a legacy component breaks every $: in it, and setting runes: true in the config breaks them everywhere. Values…

item.title: Svelte 5: Cannot export state from a module if it is reassigned
item.description: In a .svelte.js or .svelte.ts module, $state works because the compiler rewrites every read and write of that variable inside the file. Other files that import it only get the value it had, so if the module ever reassigns it (count = 0, user = null) importers would be left holding a stale copy…

item.title: Svelte: `getContext(...)` can only be used during component initialisation
item.description: Context functions and lifecycle hooks (getContext, setContext, onMount, onDestroy) attach to whichever component is being created at that moment, so they only work synchronously at the top level of a component's script. Called inside an event handler, after an await, in a setTimeout, or from a…

item.title: VMware Workstation and Device/Credential Guard are not compatible
item.description: Older VMware Workstation and Player builds need VT-x to themselves, and Credential Guard, Memory Integrity (HVCI) and Windows Sandbox all start the Hyper-V hypervisor underneath Windows, which claims it first. Workstation 15.5.5 and later can run on top of the Windows Hypervisor Platform instead…

item.title: Windows: System error 53 has occurred. The network path was not found.
item.description: net use, or Explorer, could not reach an SMB server by that name at all, so this is name resolution or TCP port 445, not permissions (those come back as error 5 or 86). The usual suspects: a hostname that only resolves through NetBIOS or LLMNR, which many networks now disable; a firewall, VPN or…

item.title: Windows: The semaphore timeout period has expired (0x80070079)
item.description: Despite the wording, this has nothing to do with semaphores in your code: Windows gave up waiting for an I/O operation, and error 121 is what the storage or network stack reports when a device stops answering. Copying to a NAS or mapped drive, it usually points at the network path (flaky Wi-Fi…

item.title: wsl: A localhost proxy configuration was detected but not mirrored into WSL
item.description: Windows has a proxy set at 127.0.0.1 or localhost, usually from a corporate VPN client, Fiddler or a tool such as Clash, and WSL 2 tried to copy it into Linux as HTTP_PROXY. In the default NAT networking mode, localhost inside WSL is the Linux VM rather than Windows, so that address would lead…

item.title: xcode-select: error: tool 'xcodebuild' requires Xcode, but active developer
item.description: The active developer directory points at the standalone Command Line Tools in /Library/Developer/CommandLineTools, which include compilers and git but not xcodebuild, simulators or platform SDKs. It happens when the tools were installed before Xcode, or a script ran xcode-select --install, and…

item.title: Xcode: SDK does not contain 'libarclite' at the path
item.description: Xcode 14.3 removed libarclite, the small library that let ARC code run on very old OS versions, so any target whose deployment target is below what current Xcode supports now fails to link. Your app target is usually fine. The culprit is a CocoaPods dependency whose podspec still declares iOS 8 or…

item.title: Zeitwerk::NameError: expected file app/models/user.rb to define constant User
item.description: Since Rails 7, Zeitwerk is the only autoloader, and it maps every file path to exactly one constant name. The file exists, but the class inside it is named something else: a typo, a module nesting that does not match the folders, or an acronym such as HTMLParser in html_parser.rb, which Zeitwerk…

item.title: (Mix) You're trying to run :my_app on Elixir v1.15.7 but it has declared
item.description: The elixir: requirement in mix.exs (for example "~> 1.17") does not match the Elixir on your PATH. It works on your laptop and fails in CI or a container because the two have different Elixir installs, often an asdf or mise .tool-versions file that the build image ignores. Remember Elixir and OTP…

item.title: /usr/bin/env: 'python': No such file or directory
item.description: The script's shebang asks for a command called python, and current Debian, Ubuntu, Fedora and macOS releases only ship python3. Python 3 is installed; there is just no executable with the bare name. It also catches scripts saved with Windows line endings, where env looks for 'python\r' and the…

item.title: AAPT: error: resource android:attr/lStar not found
item.description: android:attr/lStar was added in API 31, and a dependency (usually androidx.core 1.7 or newer, pulled in transitively) references it. Your compileSdk is older than 31, so the build tools cannot find the attribute. It looks like a broken library but is a version mismatch, and it commonly appears…

item.title: Android Gradle plugin requires Java 17 to run. You are currently using Java 11
item.description: AGP 8 needs JDK 17 to run Gradle itself, separate from the Java version your app code targets. Android Studio bundles a suitable JDK, which is why the build works in the IDE and fails on the command line or in CI, where JAVA_HOME still points at Java 11. Raising sourceCompatibility does nothing…

item.title: Android: Namespace not specified. Specify a namespace in the module's build file
item.description: Android Gradle Plugin 8 stopped reading the package attribute from AndroidManifest.xml and requires namespace in build.gradle instead. Your own module is easy to fix; the harder case is an old third-party library or Flutter or React Native plugin that has not been updated, which fails the build…

item.title: AWS Load Balancer Controller: couldn't auto-discover subnets
item.description: The controller builds an ALB by finding subnets tagged for load balancers, and none in the cluster's VPC carry the tag. Public ALBs need kubernetes.io/role/elb=1 and internal ones kubernetes.io/role/internal-elb=1. eksctl tags subnets it creates, so this usually appears on clusters built with…

item.title: bash: ulimit: open files: cannot modify limit: Operation not permitted
item.description: An unprivileged shell can lower its soft limit or raise it up to the hard limit, but never past the hard limit. Running ulimit -n 65535 asks for more than the hard limit your session inherited. Editing limits.conf does nothing for services, which take their limits from systemd, and only applies to…

item.title: C++: error: invalid use of incomplete type 'class Foo'
item.description: The compiler has seen a forward declaration of Foo but not its definition, and this line needs the full layout: calling a member, taking sizeof, holding it by value or deleting it. Headers often forward-declare on purpose to cut compile times, so the fix is to include the real header in the .cpp…

item.title: Celery: Received unregistered task of type 'myapp.tasks.send_email'
item.description: The worker took a message off the queue but has never imported the module that defines the task, so it has no idea what to run. The producer and the worker disagree about the task's name or code: the worker was started with a different -A app, autodiscovery missed the module, the task was renamed…

item.title: cert-manager: Failed to determine a valid solver configuration
item.description: None of the solvers on the Issuer matches the domains being requested, so cert-manager has no way to attempt a challenge. Solvers can be limited with a selector by dnsNames, dnsZones or labels, and a new hostname, a wildcard needing DNS01 while only HTTP01 is configured, or an Ingress pointing at…

item.title: CMake Error: Compatibility with CMake < 3.5 has been removed from CMake.
item.description: CMake 4.0 dropped support for projects that declare cmake_minimum_required below 3.5. The code is unchanged; your CMake upgraded, often silently through Homebrew, pip or a CI image, and an old project or vendored dependency still says VERSION 2.8 or 3.1. Usually the fix belongs upstream, and in…

item.title: CPU0: Core temperature above threshold, cpu clock throttled
item.description: The CPU hit its thermal limit and the hardware cut its clock speed to cool down. Everything still works, just slower, so it shows up as a benchmark or build that is fast for a minute and then degrades, or a server that is slower in summer. The cause is physical more often than not: clogged fans…

item.title: Discord API: 50013 Missing Permissions
item.description: The bot is in the server but lacks a permission for this action in this place. Discord evaluates role permissions and then channel overwrites, so a role can grant Send Messages server-wide while one channel denies it. Moderation actions add role hierarchy on top: a bot cannot kick, ban or change…

item.title: dnsmasq: failed to create listening socket for port 53: Address already in use
item.description: Something else already owns port 53. On Ubuntu and Fedora that is almost always the systemd-resolved stub listener on 127.0.0.53, and on desktops it can be a second dnsmasq started by NetworkManager or libvirt. Because dnsmasq binds the wildcard address by default, it collides even though the…

item.title: Ecto: could not lookup Ecto repo MyApp.Repo because it was not started
item.description: Ecto found the repo module but no running process registered under it. The code is fine; it is running somewhere the application tree has not been started: a Mix task, a release eval command, a seeds script run with plain elixir, or an ExUnit test helper that skipped…

item.title: Elixir: function :crypto.hmac/3 is undefined or private
item.description: OTP 24 removed the old crypto API, so :crypto.hmac/3 no longer exists. Your own code rarely calls it directly: the usual culprit is an old version of a dependency (an outdated plug_crypto, a JWT or AWS signing library) that still does. The project compiled fine on OTP 23, which is why it breaks…

item.title: GraphQL: Field "user" of type "User" must have a selection of subfields
item.description: The field returns an object type, and GraphQL never returns a whole object implicitly: you have to name the scalar fields you want inside braces. The reverse mistake, adding braces to a scalar or enum field, gives a matching "must not have a selection" error. It tends to appear after a schema…

item.description: Validation rejected the query before any resolver ran because the schema has no argument with that name on that field. It is often a client written against a different schema version, a Relay-style first/after query sent to a server that paginates with limit/offset, or a field that takes its…

item.title: INFO: task kworker blocked for more than 120 seconds
item.description: The hung task detector found a process stuck in uninterruptible sleep (D state) for two minutes, almost always waiting on I/O. The task it names is the victim, not the cause: look at the storage behind it. Typical culprits are an NFS or iSCSI server that went away, a saturated or failing disk, or…

item.description: Consumer groups and transactions need the internal __consumer_offsets topic, and the broker cannot find a healthy leader for the partition that owns your group. On a fresh single-broker dev cluster the classic cause is offsets.topic.replication.factor left at its default of 3, so the topic can…

item.description: ingress-nginx serves its built-in self-signed certificate whenever it cannot match the request to a usable TLS secret. The secret may be missing or in a different namespace from the Ingress, the hostname in spec.tls may not match spec.rules, or the client is not sending SNI at all. cert-manager…

item.title: LeakSanitizer: detected memory leaks
item.description: LeakSanitizer runs when the process exits and reports heap blocks that nothing points to any more. It is on by default with AddressSanitizer on Linux, which is why it starts failing tests the day someone enables -fsanitize=address. Direct leaks are the ones to fix first; indirect leaks are usually…

item.title: nf_conntrack: table full, dropping packet
item.description: The kernel tracks every connection passing through netfilter, and that table has a fixed size. Once it fills, new connections are silently dropped, which looks like random timeouts under load rather than an error. It is common on busy load balancers, NAT gateways and Kubernetes nodes where…

item.title: nginx: no resolver defined to resolve backend.example.com
item.description: When proxy_pass contains a variable, nginx resolves the hostname at request time instead of at startup, and that needs its own resolver directive: it does not read /etc/resolv.conf. People add the variable on purpose so nginx starts even when the backend is down, or so it picks up DNS changes…

item.description: nginx reached the HTTPS backend but the TLS handshake failed, and the usual reason surprises people: nginx does not send SNI to upstreams by default. item.title: RabbitMQ: ACCESS_REFUSED - Login was refused using authentication mechanism
item.description: The broker rejected the username and password, but the credentials are not always what is wrong. The default guest user is restricted to localhost, so guest/guest works on your machine and fails from another container or host. item.title: S3: SlowDown: Please reduce your request rate (503)
item.description: S3 is throttling requests to one key prefix, not your whole account. Each prefix supports around 3,500 writes and 5,500 reads a second, and a burst that lands on a single prefix (every object under logs/2026-10-17/, say) hits that ceiling while the rest of the bucket is idle. item.title: S3: The requested bucket name is not available (BucketAlreadyExists)
item.description: Bucket names are global across every AWS account in a partition, so somebody else already owns this one, possibly years ago. item.description: The bot token is valid and has chat:write, but the app has not been added to the channel it is posting to. item.description: The request reached Squid and Squid itself refused it: the destination site is fine. item.title: Structure needs cleaning
item.description: This is EUCLEAN, the kernel saying the filesystem found corrupt metadata and refused to trust it. On XFS and ext4 it usually follows an unclean shutdown, a failing disk or a virtual disk that lost writes. item.description: sudo wanted a password but had no terminal to ask on, because the command ran over ssh without a TTY, from cron, in a CI job or inside an Ansible or Docker step. item.description: Apollo Server 4 turns on CSRF prevention by default. It refuses GET requests and "simple" POSTs (form-encoded, multipart or text/plain) unless they carry a header a browser cannot add cross-site without a preflight. item.description: The request is fine; the account is still on a trial, and trials may only message numbers verified on that account. item.description: systemd-resolved probes each upstream server for EDNS0 and DNSSEC support and steps down when replies look broken. item.description: Ansible had to guess which Python to run modules with on the managed host, and warns because a later package install could change the answer. item.description: Ansible searched its role path and found no directory with that name. item.description: Lambda found and loaded the file named in the handler setting, but that file has no export called handler. A plain row from the database has none of them, so the error appears when the…

item.title: GraphQL: Cannot query field "email" on type "User"
item.description: The server's schema has no field by that name on that type, so the query fails validation before any resolver runs. When the field plainly exists in the code, the client is talking to another deployment, a gateway with an old supergraph, or it generated its types from a stale schema. A union or…

item.title: Loki: Maximum active stream limit exceeded, reduce the number of active streams
item.description: Every unique set of labels is its own stream in Loki, and the tenant has gone over its stream limit. That nearly always means a high cardinality value got into the labels, such as a request ID, user ID, pod hash or full path. Raising the limit only postpones the problem. Move the value out of the…

item.title: Microsoft Graph: Authorization_RequestDenied, Insufficient privileges
item.description: The app's token lacks the Graph permission this call needs. Usually it was added in the portal but admin consent was never granted, or it was added as a delegated permission while the app authenticates as itself and needs the application permission. A token issued before consent will not pick up…

item.title: mount: wrong fs type, bad option, bad superblock on /dev/sdb1
item.description: mount gives this one generic message for several unrelated failures, and the real reason is only in the kernel log. For NFS or CIFS it nearly always means the helper package (nfs-common or cifs-utils) is not installed. For a block device it is usually a disk that was never formatted, the wrong -t…

item.title: perf: Access to performance monitoring and observability operations is limited
item.description: The kernel's perf_event_paranoid setting stops unprivileged users profiling, and most distributions ship it at 2, while Debian and Ubuntu kernels carry a patch for stricter levels that block it entirely. In a container the setting comes from the host kernel and the seccomp profile also blocks…

item.title: Prometheus: many-to-many matching not allowed: matching labels must be unique
item.description: You combined two vectors with a binary operator and on the labels Prometheus matched on, both sides had more than one series. Each result has to come from exactly one pair. The query may have worked for weeks and then broken when a second instance, a restarted pod or a new label value added…

item.title: Prometheus: vector cannot contain metrics with the same labelset
item.description: A function such as rate(), or a label_replace() call, dropped the metric name or rewrote a label, so two series that used to differ now have identical labels. A query result cannot hold two series with the same labels. It usually shows up when a selector matches several metric names with a regex…

item.title: RabbitMQ: PRECONDITION_FAILED - delivery acknowledgement on channel 1 timed out
item.description: A consumer held a message unacknowledged for longer than consumer_timeout, 30 minutes by default, so the broker closed the channel and requeued the message. The consumer may be fine but slow, or it may have hung. Because the message goes back on the queue, a long job can end up processed several…

item.title: Slow DNS in Kubernetes pods: each lookup tries every search domain first
item.description: Pods get ndots:5 in resolv.conf, so any name with fewer than five dots, api.example.com included, is first tried with every cluster search domain appended. One external lookup becomes six or more queries, doubled for A and AAAA. Under load that adds latency and conntrack races that look like…

item.title: Stripe: No such customer; a similar object exists in test mode
item.description: The ID is real, but it belongs to the other mode. Test and live data in Stripe are entirely separate, so an ID saved during testing cannot be used with a live key. This usually appears straight after going live, when the database still holds customer or price IDs created against the test key.

item.title: System.Text.Json: A possible object cycle was detected
item.description: The serialiser followed references round in a circle, typically an EF Core entity whose navigation property points back at its parent, and stopped at a depth of 64. Newtonsoft.Json shows the same problem as a self referencing loop. Returning entities straight from a controller is what usually…

item.title: The bucket you are attempting to access must be addressed using the specified
item.description: This is S3's PermanentRedirect. The bucket exists, but in a different region from the endpoint the client sent the request to. The credentials and the bucket policy are fine. It usually turns up when a client defaults to us-east-1, or a hard-coded endpoint survives after the bucket was recreated…

item.title: watchdog: BUG: soft lockup - CPU#3 stuck for 22s!
item.description: A CPU spent over twice the watchdog threshold in kernel code without letting the scheduler run. On physical hardware that points to a driver or kernel bug. On a virtual machine it is usually the host: the vCPU was not scheduled because the host is overcommitted, or the guest was paused for a…

item.title: Airflow: Broken DAG: [/opt/airflow/dags/etl.py] No module named 'x'
item.description: The DAG processor could not import the file, so the DAG vanishes from the UI and a red banner appears instead. The module is missing from the environment the scheduler or DAG processor runs in, which is often not the one you tested in: a package installed in the webserver image only, or a helper…

item.title: AWS Lambda: The runtime parameter of nodejs16.x is no longer supported
item.description: The runtime has passed its deprecation date and Lambda now blocks creating or updating functions that use it. Existing functions keep running, which is why the failure appears on an unrelated code change: the deploy touches the function configuration and the old runtime string is rejected. Bumping…

item.title: AWS Lambda: TooManyRequestsException: Rate Exceeded.
item.description: Lambda refused the invocation because the function hit its concurrency ceiling, which is the account's regional limit (1,000 by default, lower on new accounts) or the function's own reserved concurrency. It is a limit on requests running at the same moment, not requests per second, so a function…

item.title: Bundler: Your bundle only supports platforms ["arm64-darwin-23"]
item.description: Gemfile.lock records the platforms it was resolved for, and it was generated on a Mac, so the Linux CI runner or Docker image is not on the list. Bundler refuses rather than guess, because platform-specific gems such as nokogiri and ffi ship different binaries. The fix is to add the target…

item.title: C++: /lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libstdc++.so.6: version `GLIBCXX_3.4.32' not found
item.description: The binary was built with a newer GCC than the machine it is running on, and it needs a libstdc++ symbol version the system library does not have. Nothing is wrong with the code: it works on the build box because that box has the newer library. It shows up when copying binaries to an older distro…

item.title: C++: error: use of deleted function
item.description: The code tries to call a function that has been explicitly deleted, and nine times out of ten that function is a copy constructor. Types such as std::unique_ptr, std::thread and std::mutex cannot be copied, so passing one by value, pushing it into a vector or capturing it in a lambda by copy…

item.title: C++: pure virtual method called, terminate called without an active exception
item.description: A pure virtual function was called through an object whose derived part does not exist at that moment. It almost always means a virtual call from a base class constructor or destructor, where the object is only the base type, or a call on an object that another thread has already started…

item.title: Cloudflare Workers: Error 1102: Worker exceeded resource limits
item.description: The Worker used more CPU time or memory than its plan allows and was stopped mid-request. CPU time counts only while your code is actually computing, so waiting on fetch() is free, but parsing a large JSON body, hashing or rendering a big page is not. A Worker that runs fine in development can hit…

item.title: CloudFront: 502 ERROR The request could not be satisfied (origin SSL failure)
item.description: CloudFront connected to the origin over HTTPS but the TLS negotiation failed, so it returned a 502 instead. The certificate on the origin must match the origin domain name configured in CloudFront, not the viewer's hostname, and must chain to a public CA. Pointing CloudFront at a load balancer's…

item.title: CloudFront: 504 ERROR The request could not be satisfied (origin timeout)
item.description: CloudFront reached for your origin and either could not open a connection or got no response in time, so the viewer sees a CloudFront error page. The origin often looks healthy when you test it directly, because the problem is on CloudFront's path: a security group or firewall that only allows…

item.title: Composer: Your lock file does not contain a compatible set of packages
item.description: composer install found that the versions pinned in composer.lock cannot run here, almost always because of the PHP version or a missing extension, not a problem with the lock file itself. The lock was generated on a machine with a newer PHP or with ext-intl or ext-gd installed, and the server or…

item.title: Gateway API: HTTPRoute Accepted=False, reason NoMatchingParent
item.description: The HTTPRoute names a Gateway in parentRefs, but no listener on that Gateway will take it, so the route is ignored and traffic never arrives. The usual causes are a sectionName or port that matches no listener, a hostname outside the listener's hostname, or a route in a namespace the listener's…

item.title: grep: Invalid range end
item.description: A bracket expression contains a range whose end sorts before its start. In POSIX brackets a backslash is literal, so [\w-.] means the range from w to a full stop, not a word character and a hyphen. Ranges like [a-Z] also depend on the locale's collation order, which is why the same command works…

item.title: gRPC: StatusCode.UNKNOWN, Exception calling application
item.description: The server's handler raised an exception it did not turn into a gRPC status, so the framework reported UNKNOWN (code 2) and the client learns nothing useful. The real traceback is in the server's log, not the client's. Other languages behave the same way: an uncaught Java exception or a panic…

item.title: gRPC: tls: first record does not look like a TLS handshake
item.description: The client started a TLS handshake and the server answered in plain text, which means the client uses TLS credentials and the server, or whatever is in front of it, listens without TLS. The reverse mismatch shows as the server logging a bogus greeting or an HTTP/2 frame error. A proxy that…

item.title: gRPC: UNAVAILABLE, GOAWAY received, ENHANCE_YOUR_CALM, too_many_pings
item.description: The client sent HTTP/2 keepalive pings more often than the server permits, so the server closed the connection and every call in flight failed. Client and server keepalive settings are configured separately and a client tuned to ping every few seconds will be cut off by a server using the default…

item.title: ingress-nginx: failed calling webhook "validate.nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io"
item.description: The API server tried to ask the ingress-nginx admission webhook whether your Ingress is valid and could not reach it at all, so nothing about your manifest has been judged yet. It usually means the controller pod is not running, a NetworkPolicy or private cluster firewall blocks the control plane…

item.title: ingress-nginx: host "example.com" and path "/" is already defined in ingress
item.description: The admission webhook rejected the Ingress because another Ingress, possibly in a different namespace, already claims exactly the same host and path. ingress-nginx merges every Ingress into one nginx config, so two owners for one location would be ambiguous. It often catches out a blue and green…

item.title: Keycloak: Cookie not found. Please make sure cookies are enabled
item.description: Keycloak sets a cookie when the login page loads and expects it back when the form is submitted, and it did not come back. Browsers are rarely at fault: behind a reverse proxy Keycloak often thinks it is on plain HTTP or the wrong hostname, so it issues a cookie the browser will not return…

item.title: Laravel: No application encryption key has been specified.
item.description: APP_KEY is empty in the environment Laravel actually loaded, so it cannot encrypt cookies or sessions. On a fresh clone that just means .env was never created. In production it is usually a cached config from before the key was set, or a container whose environment does not include the variable…
